fm_reference: FM24 Training screen (Schedule / Individual / Coaches / Development)
biggest_gap: No mentoring analog: FM24's Training area includes a Mentoring tab where senior players are grouped with youngsters to transfer traits, professionalism and development pace; Game A even flags veterans as 'stagnating - consider Move Practice or a successor' but gives them no developmental role. Fix: add a Mentoring section to the Training screen - pair a veteran (age_mult<=0.7) with 1-2 young Pokemon (compatible type); mentored juniors get a visible development multiplier and an accelerated pipeline to learn one move from the mentor's moveset, the veteran gains morale/purpose, with effects applied in the daily tick and surfaced in Development.

history.gap: Schedule is a fixture-blind repeating weekly template with no matchday awareness or calendar integration, unlike FM24's fixture-embedded training calendar.
Training load is squad-uniform — no per-Pokémon intensity/rest control or auto rules tied to strain/age, unlike FM24's per-player training intensity with condition-based automation.

Schedule editing is template-only: you edit one repeating weekday template (plus automatic fixture overrides), so you cannot plan specific future weeks differently — no way to lay down a deliberate recovery week before a congested block, a heavy pre-season/free-week development block, or opponent-specific prep for one big fixture, the way FM24's Calendar lets you edit each actual upcoming week (with presets applicable per-week and a multi-week view). Fix: make the visible calendar per-date editable (template as default, date-level overrides stored like {date: {am,pm,intensity}}), add a 2-4 week view, and let presets apply to a chosen future week.

No mentoring analog: FM24's Training area includes a Mentoring tab where senior players are grouped with youngsters to transfer traits, professionalism and development pace; Game A even flags veterans as 'stagnating - consider Move Practice or a successor' but gives them no developmental role. Fix: add a Mentoring section to the Training screen - pair a veteran (age_mult<=0.7) with 1-2 young Pokemon (compatible type); mentored juniors get a visible development multiplier and an accelerated pipeline to learn one move from the mentor's moveset, the veteran gains morale/purpose, with effects applied in the daily tick and surfaced in Development.

fix_round1: Schedule is now a real dated calendar (today..+6) with the player's fixtures embedded as amber cells; effective_plan() auto-adjusts around fixtures (matchday = warm-up + MATCH only, day after = enforced recovery, day before = light + Match Prep that raises condition); matches add real strain to likely starters; projections, net-strain row, session counts and move-learn rate all computed over the fixture-adjusted week; auto-adjust toggle persisted.
round2_notes: Round 1 gap convincingly fixed and verified live via driver (artifacts/training/round2/*.png): fixture embeds in the week, matchday/post-match/pre-match cells lock correctly, manual override warns and spikes net strain (+11), move learning progressed 16%->73% over advanced days, Development tab shows real 28-day stat deltas and IV gains, coaches workload/multipliers wired. All four tabs live, persistent, coherent. Remaining deficit is per-individual workload control.
fix_round2: Per-Pokémon workload added end-to-end: every Pokémon has its own training load (Automatic / Double / High / Normal / Light / Half / No Training). Automatic is condition-tied automation — full rest at strain>=78, Light at >=60, veterans capped at Normal and eased to Light from 45, fresh (<25) rapid developers pushed to High. The effective step scales that individual's development points (x0..x1.5), strain intake (x0..x1.9) and move-learning drills (paused on No Training) in the daily tick, projections, ETAs and the 7-day personal strain forecast. Surfaced as an editable Load dropdown per row in the Squad Training Status table (with 7d-delta column), a Load column in the Individual list, and a full TRAINING WORKLOAD section in the detail panel (auto-rule explanation, multipliers, what Automatic would do instead). Visible pushback: forced heavy loads at high strain drain morale, raise knock risk (x1.5 on Double) and send 'unhappy with workload' inbox complaints; fresh rapid developers held on Half/No Training complain they want to train more; both appear in Development > Needs attention. Verified: dev_check asserts auto rules and that a rested Pokémon gains 0 stats over 42 days while a Doubled one develops fastest with the most strain; screenshots artifacts/training/fix2/*.png show auto->Light engaged at 60%, a forced-Double Tauros at 100% strain reacting badly, a rested Dodrio wanting more, and the inbox complaints. Note: smoke.sh currently fails only on res://screens/transfers/screen.gd parse errors (another builder mid-edit); headless boot shows zero errors from training files and SIM CHECK OK.
round3_notes: Round 2 gap convincingly fixed and verified live (artifacts/training/round3/*.png + drivers): per-mon loads editable in the status table, auto rules resolve per strain/age (auto->High for fresh Dodrio, auto->Normal for vets), forced Double on Tauros shows +21 7d-delta warning, focus Speed lifts projection to 12.8 pts/wk, Body Slam pipeline 0%->ETA 35d with Cancel, 18 advanced days produced real stat deltas/IV gains and inbox messages. Screen is now close to FM24 parity; secondary observations: no mentoring analog (FM24 Training has a Mentoring tab — veteran->youngster growth/trait transfer would map beautifully), no attribute progress graphs despite snapshots being stored, right-rail session counts truncate at 1600px, monograms not sprites. Verdict was narrow: information density and liveness already match or beat FM24.
fix_round3: Per-date calendar planning added end-to-end, FM24-Calendar style. The Schedule tab is now a 1/2/4-week dated calendar (view toggle persisted) where EVERY cell (AM/PM session, intensity) edits that specific DATE as an override on top of the weekday template; overridden slots get a violet border and a dot on the date header, with tooltips showing the template default and a '↺ Template default' entry to reset. Three-layer resolution in effective_plan(): template -> per-date override -> fixture auto-adjust, with deliberate date plans BEATING the pre/post-match auto defaults while the matchday itself stays locked. Each visible week has a Plan ▾ menu: stamp any of the 6 presets onto JUST that week (7 dated overrides, template untouched — recovery week before a congested block, heavy development block in a free week, prep week), reset week to template, or save the week AS the new template (bakes overrides in and consumes them). NEW this pass: one-click opponent prep for a single big fixture — a Prep button on each upcoming fixture in the right rail calls plan_prep_for_fixture(), laying light Match-Prep-heavy dated plans on the ≤3 days into that match (skipping other matchdays; Match Prep raises condition which the sim rates battlers by, so it is a real edge). Right rail lists 'Planned days · next 28' with per-date reset buttons; overrides are pruned automatically once their date has run; all projections (net strain row, weekly projection, ETAs, session counts, move-learn rate) read the override-resolved plan, and the daily tick trains exactly what the calendar shows. Also fixed: rested individuals' match-prep strain projection now matches the actual tick (-6), and calendar cells no longer overflow at 1600px (fit_to_longest_item off, 112px cells — all 7 days visible). Verified: dev_check asserts single-date override wins over template and does not leak, deliberate plan beats post-match auto, matchday stays locked against edits, week preset lays 7 dated plans without touching the template, clear-week drops them, save-week-as-template bakes them, opponent prep plans a double-prep eve without touching the template, and past-date overrides are pruned after 42 advanced days — DEV CHECK OK. smoke.sh SMOKE OK; screenshot artifacts/training/fix3/training.png shows the 2-week calendar with a single-date edit, a Heavy Development week stamped on week+1, opponent prep planned into the 17 Oct fixture (violet cells/dots), Plan ▾ menus, Prep buttons and the planned-days rail — all live from user://training.json.
round4_notes: Round 3 gap convincingly fixed and verified live (artifacts/training/round4/*.png): per-date calendar edits (violet cells + dots + reset), week Plan menus stamping presets on one week, one-click opponent Prep laying Match-Prep days into a fixture, planned-days rail with per-date resets - all persisted in user://training.json and honored by the daily tick. Deeper-state driver verified: move dialog with learnset/power/type, Waterfall pipeline 0% with ~31d ETA, forced Double load showing manual-override panel and what Automatic would do, coach workload penalties (-7% at 3 areas), and 12 advanced days producing real stat deltas, IV gains, weekly training report + knock/complaint messages in inbox. All four tabs live; density on Schedule arguably exceeds FM24 (per-day net strain economics, per-mon 7d strain forecast). FM24 wins narrowly on functional depth: no Mentoring (biggest gap), plus secondary deltas - session vocabulary is 7 focus types vs FM's ~30+ session library with unit assignments and set-piece/tactical-familiarity payoffs, no attribute progress graphs despite 70 days of stored snapshots, no per-session training performance ratings, monograms instead of sprites, occasional label truncation (Move Practi, Veteran - minimal gr...). Also cosmetic: shell sub-nav highlight can desync from the active tab when switched programmatically (driver artifact, not user-reachable).
